title: Shadow traffic PRD notes (working) — quality metrics during rollouts
content:
Context / why this exists
- Console & Rollouts is good for latency/cost/error, but we don’t have a first-class way to measure quality regressions during a rollout without exposing users.
- Repeated ask from enterprise / Dedicated: “We can’t upgrade models unless we can prove quality didn’t regress.” (ref: SUP-28451)
- Proposed solution: shadow traffic. Sample production requests, mirror to candidate variants, score asynchronously, display deltas + confidence, attach to canary/A-B decisions.

Working name(s)
- “Shadow Experiments” (Console)
- “Shadow traffic quality metrics” (PRD)
- “Quality deltas in rollouts” (UX)

Non-negotiables (notes from SRE + platform leadership)
- Must be fail-open: shadow path failure cannot impact control response.
- Must not meaningfully impact tail latency on user path.
- Must not explode telemetry cardinality.
- Must have data minimization + retention defaults that work for Dedicated + Private.

Assumptions (version as of 2026-02-12)
- v1 is Redwood-provided metrics + rubric templates; no customer code execution in our env.
- Customers can “bring prompt sets” via eval-harness separately; shadow path focuses on live prod sampling.
- We will support Hosted + Dedicated + Private from a config / API perspective, but beta will likely be Dedicated only.


1) User problems (raw notes)
- Platform Eng: “I want to try a new quantization profile / routing policy but need a safety net.”
- ML Eng: “My offline evals don’t match production; I need real traffic signals.”
- Product/QA: “We ship rollouts; we need a regression gate, not just latency.”

Jobs-to-be-done
- Compare control vs candidate outputs on the same request distribution.
- Understand deltas by segment (route, model, region, request type) without over-filtering into noise.
- Drill into examples when a metric moves.
- Know if the measurement is trustworthy (sample size, CI, scoring lag).


2) What we’re building (rough scope)
Control Plane / Routing
- Shadow policy attached to a route and/or rollout (rollout preferred to keep it “experiment-shaped”).
- Sampling controls: percent, deterministic bucketing (stable across time windows), optional per-route cap.
- Targets: 1+ candidate variants (new model version, quant profile, prompt template, routing policy).
- Headers/metadata: define what gets mirrored; strip or hash sensitive identifiers.
- Fail-open rules: strict timeouts to shadow targets; don’t propagate errors; circuit breaker when unhealthy.

Telemetry + Data
- “Shadow pair” event capturing (control request, control output ref, candidate output ref, timing, outcome).
- Store minimal required data by default (hashes + short snippets) and keep full prompt/response behind explicit flags.
- Retention: short by default; configurable for Dedicated/Private.

Scoring
- Async queue, batch scoring.
- Default rubric set (v1): safety/refusal, format adherence, instruction-following proxy, “helpfulness” rubric (model-graded) (exact list TBD in PM-1843).
- Stats: compute deltas + confidence intervals; guard against Simpson’s paradox (basic segmentation guidance).

Console
- Create shadow experiment, view results, attach to rollout timeline.
- Charts: delta over time + CI band; show “insufficient samples” state.
- Example drilldown: show request + control vs shadow outputs + metric breakdown.
- Alerts: quality regression thresholds, scoring lag, shadow target errors.


3) What’s explicitly out-of-scope (v1)
- Full offline replay system for arbitrary historical windows.
- Customer-supplied code execution (scorers) in Redwood worker environment.
- “Replace control response with shadow response” (this is not a traffic switch).
- Fully automated rollback based on quality signals (launch as advisory unless we’re extremely confident).


4) Open questions (big ones)
Experiment semantics
- Is a “shadow experiment” always tied to a rollout object? Or can it be standalone on a route?
  - leaning: support both; beta UX anchors to rollouts.
- How many candidate variants do we allow concurrently?
  - gut: 1–3; avoid combinatorial reporting + cost.
- Deterministic bucketing inputs: which fields can we include without privacy risk?
  - likely: stable request fingerprint using route_id + user-provided request_id (if present) + hashed payload features (TBD by platform). Need guardrails and a “salt per tenant”.
- What’s the experience for streaming requests?
  - we can’t mirror token-by-token cheaply; likely capture final assembled prompt + “first N tokens” of response; or terminate shadow after N tokens.

Metrics / scoring
- Which metrics are “safe defaults” and won’t cause immediate false alarms?
  - format adherence is good; refusal rate maybe; “helpfulness” is subjective and prompt-dependent.
- How do we calibrate model-graded rubrics across model versions (grader drift)?
  - require pinned rubric version + pinned grader model version; show this prominently.
- How do we handle “control response error” cases?
  - likely exclude from quality scoring; still count in denominator for paired sampling completeness.
- Do we support “exact match” metrics for structured outputs?
  - might be important for tool calling / JSON schema compliance.

Data handling
- Default retention by plan (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) needs decision.
- Default redaction: allowlist fields vs regex? (security wants allowlist-first.)
- For Dedicated: do we allow customer to opt into storing full prompt/response for X days? (Yes, but needs explicit knob + audit.)
- For Private: can scoring run fully inside customer environment? Or export-only?
  - likely: v1 supports local scoring workers as optional package; otherwise customers can export artifacts and score externally.

Performance / cost
- Budgeting: what is the max incremental cost (telemetry + scoring) we can tolerate?
- Do we enforce an org-level “shadow token budget” (per hour/day)?
- How to communicate cost in the UI (estimated tokens/day and scoring compute)?

Rollout automation
- Advisory-only at launch? If we add auto-rollback later, what guardrails?
  - likely: advisory-only for GA, with optional “block promotion” mode for canaries (no automatic rollback).


5) Prioritization notes (v1 must-haves vs nice-to-haves)
Must-haves for beta (Dedicated)
- Deterministic sampling + 1 candidate variant.
- Fail-open routing w/ timeouts + circuit breaker.
- Telemetry event schema that won’t blow up Prom/ClickHouse/etc.
- Basic scoring pipeline (at least 2–3 metrics) + CI.
- Console: results table + one delta chart + scoring lag indicator + examples list (even if basic).
- Kill switch + runbook + oncall dashboards.

Nice-to-haves
- Multiple candidates.
- Segment builder (powerful filters) and saved segments.
- Export to CSV/JSON for offline analysis.
- Auto-stop criteria (power-based early stop).
- A/B + shadow combined view.

Explicit “no” for beta
- Custom metric code.
- Full prompt/response retention by default.


6) Beta customer candidates (working list)
Selection criteria
- Dedicated tenant (so we can control config + retention and have stable traffic).
- Has active rollouts planned (model upgrade / quant change) in next 4–8 weeks.
- Will tolerate “beta rough edges” and join weekly check-ins.
- Has clear success criterion (e.g., approve a model upgrade) so we can measure impact.

Candidates (from CS/Sales notes)
- Northstar (customer-support AI platform) — strong need for quality gates during upgrades; asks for refusal/safety + instruction-following; high urgency (ref: Fireflies 2026-01-22; HubSpot company-northstar-customer-support-ai).
- Aurora Devtools — high-volume, cost-sensitive; wants proof to switch to cheaper model/quant; good for testing overhead + sampling tradeoffs (HubSpot company-aurora-devtools).
- HelioFin RegTech — regulated; excellent for retention/redaction/audit requirements but might be too strict for early beta unless we have knobs fully ready (HubSpot company-heliofin-regtech).

Beta “shape” proposal
- Beta wave 1 (2 customers): Northstar + Aurora.
- Beta wave 2 (1 customer): HelioFin only if security controls are in place; otherwise defer to post-beta.


7) Rough UX sketches (text)
Create flow (Console)
1) Entry points
   - From Rollout detail page: “Add shadow experiment” (preferred)
   - From Route settings: “Shadow testing” tab

2) Step-by-step wizard (minimal)
   Step A: Choose control + candidate
   - Control: (pre-filled from route/rollout)
   - Candidate: select “variant” (model version / quant profile / routing policy / prompt template)
   - Show cost estimate: “~X mirrored requests/day; ~Y tokens/day; scoring lag estimate”

   Step B: Sampling
   - Sampling rate (%) with recommended defaults (e.g., 0.5% / 1% / 5% depending on traffic)
   - Deterministic bucketing toggle (default ON)
   - Safety limit: max mirrored RPS (optional advanced)

   Step C: Data handling
   - Default: “store hashed identifiers + truncated prompt excerpt + truncated outputs”
   - Advanced toggles: store full prompt/response for N days (if plan allows)
   - Redaction profile: default allowlist; show warning that regex is best-effort

   Step D: Metrics
   - Default bundle v1 (checkboxes; show “recommended”)
   - Rubric version pinning (auto)

   Step E: Review + enable
   - Summary panel + warnings
   - Show fail-open behavior (“does not affect user response”)

Results page
- Top summary cards
  - Sample size (paired), time window
  - Scoring lag (p50/p95)
  - Shadow target error rate
  - “Data coverage” (what fraction had usable shadow outputs)

- Deltas table (control vs candidate)
  - Metric name | control | candidate | delta | CI | status (improve/regress/insufficient)

- Chart
  - One metric selected -> delta over time + CI band

- Drilldowns
  - “View examples” -> list of paired samples with metric highlights
  - Filters: route, model, region (keep extremely limited in v1 to reduce cardinality risk)

Attach to rollout
- On rollout timeline: “Shadow experiment enabled @ t0” and show the current “quality status” next to latency/cost.
- Promotion gating (v1): show advisory banner: “Quality regression detected (format adherence -1.4pp, 95% CI [-2.1, -0.6]). Consider pausing rollout.”

Copy / warnings (from DES-613 notes)
- “Shadow traffic duplicates a sample of requests to a candidate configuration. Users always receive the control response.”
- “Shadow results may lag behind real time due to async scoring.”
- “Some metrics are proxies and may require calibration for your domain.”


8) Success criteria (for PRD, but jotting here)
Beta success
- 2+ Dedicated customers run shadow testing during a real rollout decision.
- At least 1 case where quality regression is caught before impact (or an upgrade is approved with confidence).
- Shadow path overhead: no measurable impact on control p99 beyond agreed budget; zero sev incidents.
- Telemetry cardinality within budget; no repeated “metrics cardinality” escalations (ref: SUP-28510).

GA success (later)
- % of rollouts using shadow testing.
- Reduction in time-to-approve model upgrades.
- Fewer quality regressions shipped.


9) Risks / watch-outs (quick list)
- False positives from subjective metrics -> customers lose trust quickly.
- Grader model drift -> comparisons across time become meaningless.
- Cardinality blow-ups if we allow free-form tags (customer_id, prompt_id, etc.).
- Scoring lag -> user thinks product is broken (needs strong UI state + alerting).
- “Prompt retention creep” -> security/compliance pushback; must be conservative by default.
- Streaming semantics -> easiest place to accidentally add overhead.


10) Next actions (as of 2026-02-12)
Product (Marissa)
- Align on v1 metric bundle + wording (sync with PM-1843).
- Confirm beta wave 1 customers + start onboarding doc (PM-1844).
- Draft pricing/packaging stance (PM-1845) with rough cost model.

Design (Kenji)
- Produce updated create-flow wireframes w/ explicit cost + retention callouts.
- Define minimal results page for beta: table + 1 chart + examples.

Eng
- Console backend (Dylan/Chloe/Jada): confirm API shape; ensure rollouts integration is a pointer not duplication.
- Telemetry (Logan/Nadia): finalize event schema + dimension allowlist.
- SRE (Sean): confirm SLOs + paging; ensure runbook includes kill-switch.
- Security (Marcus/Kevin): decide default retention + audit log requirements; confirm how redaction config is exposed.


Appendix A: raw customer quotes (unfiltered)
- “We can’t flip models without proof we didn’t break customer support flows.” (Northstar)
- “Latency/cost are fine; the board cares about answer correctness. Show me confidence, not anecdotes.” (Dedicated prospect, 2026-01-22 call)
- “If I can’t control retention and audit who accessed prompts, it’s a non-starter.” (HelioFin)

Appendix B: terminology to standardize
- Shadow target vs candidate variant (pick one)
- Control vs baseline
- Paired sample vs matched request
- Scoring lag vs processing delay

(End — this doc is intentionally messy; will be folded into Confluence PRD once open questions are resolved.)
